draft.title: Generators
card: A generator turns a coil in a magnetic field. The flux through the coil keeps changing, so an emf is induced in the coil.
As the coil turns, each side moves up through the field and then down through it. The emf reverses direction every half turn, so it is alternating.
two full rings, each joined to one end of the coil. They keep the same connection to the circuit all the time, so the output is AC.
a split ring that swaps the connections every half turn. The current in the circuit then flows one way only, so the output is DC.
draft.remember: A turning coil induces an alternating emf. Slip rings pass it on as AC, and a commutator flips the connections to give DC.

a.q: Why does the emf induced in a turning generator coil alternate?
opts: Each side of the coil moves up, then down, through the field
The magnetic field reverses direction every half turn
The coil stops moving at the top of each turn
The coil switches between a field and no field
a.why: As the coil turns, each side moves through the field in one direction and then the opposite direction, so the induced emf reverses every half turn. The magnet itself does not change, so the field does not reverse.
a.clue: Think about which way each side of the coil moves through the field.

b.q: A student builds a simple generator and wants the output to be DC. Which part should be fitted to the coil?
opts: A commutator
A pair of slip rings
A second magnet
A longer coil
b.why: A commutator is a split ring that swaps the connections every half turn, so the current in the circuit flows one way. Slip rings keep the same connections, so they would give AC.
b.clue: One part swaps the connections every half turn.

a.best: Each side of the coil moves up, then down, through the field
